paper_sections.title: Brain activation patterns associated with cue reactivity and craving in abstinent problem gamblers, heavy smokers and healthy controls: an fMRI study
Results for performance data and craving ratings
Correlations between BOLD activation, subjective craving, BDI-II and CAARS

description.value: The study compared cue-related brain activation and subjective craving during gambling and smoking picture viewing in treatment-seeking problem gamblers, heavy smokers, and healthy controls, and examined associations between cue-reactivity-related activation and craving.

design.value: A functional magnetic resonance imaging event-related cue reactivity paradigm consisting of gambling, smoking-related and neutral pictures was employed in 17 treatment-seeking non-smoking problem gamblers, 18 non-gambling heavy smokers, and 17 non-gambling and non-smoking healthy controls. Exploratory analyses compared heavy smokers with high and low Fagerström Test for Nicotine Dependence scores.

task_description.value: A picture two-choice response task using gambling, smoking-related, neutral and low-level baseline pictures. Thirty pictures from each category were presented randomly. Each picture was presented for 5 seconds with a 2.5-second blank screen between pictures.

instructions.value: For gambling, smoking-related and neutral pictures, participants pressed a response button with the left index finger when a face was present and with the right index finger when no face was present. For low-level baseline pictures, participants responded left or right according to arrows. Participants were requested to respond within 5 seconds and were not encouraged to respond as quickly as possible.

stimuli.value: Thirty gambling pictures, 30 smoking-related pictures, 30 neutral pictures and 30 low-level baseline pictures. Pictures were matched for complexity and naturalistic setting; only males and neutral facial expressions were included. Low-level baseline pictures showed arrows pointing left or right.

task_performance_measures.value: Mean reaction time to the pictures in each stimulus category

modality.value: T2*-weighted echo planar images sensitive to blood oxygenation level-dependent (BOLD) contrast

instrument.value: 3.0 Tesla Philips Intera full-body fMRI scanner equipped with a standard SENSE RF head coil and Quasar gradient system, Philips Medical Systems BV, Eindhoven, the Netherlands

description.value: Thirty-five axial slices were acquired with an interslice gap of 0.3 mm, matrix size 64 × 64 mm, bandwidth 90 kHz, and coverage of the entire brain except for the inferior regions of the cerebellum. The scanning session lasted 15 minutes.

description.value: A sagittal T1-weighted structural scan with 170 slices was made in order to co-register it with the fMRI data.

Images were slice-timed, reoriented and realigned to the first volume. T1-coregistered volumes were normalized to an SPM T1-template using 12 linear parameters and a set of non-linear cosine basis functions, followed by spatial smoothing.

software.value: SPM2 (Statistical Parametric Mapping; Wellcome Department of Cognitive Neurology, London, UK)

Spatial smoothing using an 8 mm FWHM Gaussian kernel

model_settings.value: Performance data were analyzed with group as a between-subject factor and stimulus category as a within-subject factor, using group contrasts. Urge ratings were analyzed with time as a within-subject factor.

estimator.value: Tukey's post hoc tests were used for group differences in demographic and clinical data.

model_settings.value: Delta functions convolved with a synthetic hemodynamic response function were used to model responses to each stimulus type. Single-subject contrast images were generated for each comparison of interest.

Single-subject contrast images were entered into second-level random-effects analyses. Main effects and interaction effects were analyzed with one-way ANOVA. Results used a cluster-size restriction of 10 voxels at P < 0.05 corrected for multiple comparisons according to the Family Wise Error method; group interactions used a cluster-size restriction of 5 voxels at P < 0.001, masked with the appropriate main effect.

Regression analyses were performed separately for PRG and HSM to test whether activation to gambling or smoking stimuli, respectively, versus neutral pictures correlated with self-reported craving after scanning. Separate analyses tested associations with CAARS and BDI-II scores.
